label: Bouhezza
note: Made by filling a skin bag with salted lben and milk over weeks, not by packing pressed curd.

about.text: A soft, salty, semi-fat Algerian cheese of the Aurès (Chaouia) region, made from raw goat, sheep or cow milk and ripened for one to six months in a goatskin bag filled with salted lben.

links.name: Aissaoui Zitoun et al. 2022, Algerian J. Nutrition and Food Sciences 2(3)

how.label: fill the skin over weeks
how.text: Bouhezza is never pressed or cut: the skin bag is filled in layers over weeks, whey seeps out through it, and the mass ripens in the bag under its own lactic flora. It has been granted a quality-sign recognition (geographical indication process) in Algeria.

steps.name: prepare skin
steps.note: Depilated, washed, treated with salt and juniper berry, turned inside out, rinsed, then left overnight with lben.

steps.name: fill
steps.note: Salted lben, preferably skimmed and low in acidity, fills at least half the bag, with more lben and salt added over several weeks and the raw milk last.
Acidification, whey draining and ripening happen together through the permeable skin.

processing.text: No starter; salted lben is added to the skin over weeks and the indigenous flora do the work, with yeasts and moulds at 5-6 log. Cloth bags are often used instead of skin today.

Drained and ripened in a goat or sheep skin (chekoua/djeld) with repeated additions of lben; Aurès/Chaouia; Algerian process sheet gives 2-3 months, other sources only 'several weeks'; originally goat/sheep milk, cow milk now common

facts.v: Lactococcus 8.45 log cfu/ml and Lactobacillus 7.73 log cfu/ml during manufacture, yeasts and moulds 5–6 log; LAB stay 6–7 log cfu/g in the cheese
cloth bags are often used instead of skin
